team.summary: Founded by Raja Koduri, a veteran GPU architect and executive with leadership roles at Intel and AMD. Prior startup experience includes founding Mihira. Strong technical depth in hardware/silicon, but direct robotics domain experience is less documented.

founders.name: Raja Koduri
founders.background: Former senior GPU architect/executive at Intel and AMD; founded Mihira with Shobu Yarlagadda and S.S. Rajamouli.

team.technicalDepth: Exceptional — deep expertise in GPU architecture, silicon design, and hardware engineering from Intel/AMD leadership roles.

product.plainLanguage: [inferred] A deep-tech robotics and hardware company; specific product functionality not publicly described beyond the one-liner.

risks.text: High technical and execution risk in deep-tech robotics/hardware with unproven product-market fit.
Limited public information on defensibility (IP, data moats, switching costs).
Dependence on continued capital intensity; $35M Series A may not suffice for hardware scaling.
Founder's robotics-specific experience unclear; team may lack domain-specific operational experience.

subScores.label: Team
subScores.rationale: Founder has exceptional technical depth (GPU architecture at Intel/AMD) and prior startup experience (Mihira). Strong founder-market fit for deep-tech hardware, though robotics-specific experience is less evident.

subScores.label: Defensibility
subScores.rationale: No public evidence of proprietary data, workflow lock-in, network effects, or IP portfolio. Deep-tech hardware may yield patents, but dependence on single platform and switching costs are unknown.

subScores.label: Product
subScores.rationale: One-liner is vague; no demonstration of AI-native agent, self-serve onboarding, or clear product articulation. Likely early-stage hardware development with no user-facing product yet.

subScores.label: Market & Why-Now
subScores.rationale: Broad 'robotics and hardware' vertical lacks specific size hint, why-now driver (e.g., LLM cost collapse, new APIs), identifiable competitors, or stated wedge strategy.

subScores.label: Traction / Freshness
subScores.rationale: Recent $35M Series A funding signals investor confidence and provides runway. However, no public signals of paying customers, active usage, product launch, or community engagement (HN/GitHub).

scoreRationale: Oxmiq Labs benefits from a world-class founder with deep hardware expertise and fresh capital, but scores low on product clarity, market specificity, and demonstrable defensibility. The investment thesis emphasizes AI-native agents, vertical SaaS workflows, and self-serve SMB onboarding — none of which are evidenced here. The company appears to be a pre-product deep-tech hardware play, which falls outside the thesis sweet spot.
